transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Time: 14:00 - 14:58 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Alicia (AstraPay Head of Security), Ben (AstraPay Platform), Priya (Procurement), Carlos (Legal)

Summary: quick preflight before procurement submission; main topics: MSA/DPA exceptions (PCI questions), SLA tiers (latency for payments routing), KMS/HSM integration & audit logs, pricing for dedicated capacity vs hosted, data residency/egress. Agreed next steps: send security packet, schedule bench, provide pricing scenarios.

Topics:
- Security packet and attestations
- Hosted API vs Dedicated (predictable p99 vs cost)
- KMS/HSM and key custody choices (bring-your-own-key)
- DPA PCI implications & audit logs retention
- Pricing examples for committed capacity + burst

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday, appreciate it. quick round robin?
[00:08] Alicia (AstraPay - Head of Security): hi all, Alicia here. just, um, I wanna make sure we cover PCI surface and audit log retention up front.
[00:15] Ben (AstraPay - Platform Eng): Ben here. we'll cover traffic pattern and a short list of must-haves.
[00:20] Priya (Procurement): Priya, procurement lead. timeline: we need pricing and legal on same week or we pause.
[00:28] Maya: great. Jordan from our infra team will lead on the technical tradeoffs. Jordan?
[00:33] Jordan (Redwood SE): yeah hi, quick context: Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private VPC deployments. tradeoff summary: hosted is fastest to go-live but has multi-tenant egress; dedicated yields predictable p99 latency and isolation; private is for air-gapped/regulatory.
[00:50] Alicia: when you say dedicated, do you support customer-managed KEKs? we need BYOK/HSM with attestable key rotation.
[00:58] Jordan: yes, on dedicated and private we support customer KMS integrations. currently we integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and have HSM connectors for customers using external key managers. I'll send the exact architecture diagram.
[01:12] Maya: note, we have a security packet — SOC 2 type II, pen test summary, and a short HSM integration note. linking that after the call.
[01:21] Carlos (Legal): quick process q: MSA redlines — we have a couple of DPA items around data deletion timelines and subprocessor lists; any standard variance?
[01:30] Liam (CSM): from previous enterprise customers we have common concessions: limited data retention for logs, audit log export, and contractual egress fee caps. but we try to minimize DPA exceptions.
[01:45] Ben: for PCI specifically, we can't have cardholder data leaving our VPC without tokenization. What's your stance on tokenization in-flight vs at rest?
[01:55] Jordan: Redwood's runtime doesn't store raw payloads by default; with dedicated you can configure no persistence and keep KV caches in-memory. there have been occasional transcriptions that call it 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes — ignore that — but the behaviour is in-line: no persistent storage unless you opt in.
[02:15] Alicia: okay need that documented. Also, can you produce audit logs with user-level context for 3 years? our compliance team asked for 3-year retention and exportability.
[02:25] Maya: we can export audit logs; default reten is 90 days on hosted, longer retention is available as an add-on, and dedicated/private can be configured to ship logs to your S3 or SIEM. 3 years is possible, but will be an extra cost — we'll detail options.
[02:38] Priya: pricing question: what does committed capacity look like for peak vs sustained? do you charge for caching or KV cache size?
[02:45] Jordan: pricing elements: token usage for hosted, reserved GPUs for dedicated (monthly commit), and egress. KV cache is a runtime memory cost and usually baked into dedicated quotes at certain sizes; if you need large persistent caches or embeddings store, that could be extra. we'll provide scenarios: small pilot (50k req/day), mid (500k/day), prod (2M/day).
[03:10] Ben: we operate at weird spikes — payment auths can burst 20x for promos. can the dedicated pool burst while keeping p99 under 200ms?
[03:20] Jordan: yes if you provision burst capacity or autoscale policies. p99 depends on model choice and sequence length; for short payment prompts (<64 tokens) we typically see p99 ~ 120ms on our optimized LLM with batch sizing tuned. we will run a bench with your token distributions.
[03:40] Alicia: model variants — we use a deterministic small model for scoring and a bigger model for merchant messaging. can you host multiple model variants in the same dedicated pool?
[03:48] Jordan: you can pin model versions per route, and the runtime supports routing policies. mixing is fine but will affect utilization. also note quantized variants may reduce cost but need evals for regressions.
[04:02] Carlos: about SLAs — do you provide latency SLAs or just uptime? procurement needs hard SLOs for p99.
[04:10] Maya: our standard enterprise SLA covers availability and latency targets for dedicated customers in the contract; we measure token-level latencies in the console. contractually we can include p99 targets for specific routes tied to a dedicated pool, with credits for violations.
[04:26] Priya: what about indemnities and PCI carveouts? we need to align on indemnity language if there's card data leakage.
[04:34] Maya: we generally don't accept broad indemnities; we propose narrow liability caps and strong operational mitigations (no persistence, BYOK, audit logs). legal can follow up on specific clause language.
[04:45] Ben: on the tech side, what network egress should we expect — will there be cross-region routing costs if the model is in US-east but our clients are EU?
[04:54] Jordan: yes cross-region egress may apply; we can pin model serving to EU regions to avoid latency and egress fees. private deployments can run inside your VPC to eliminate cross-cloud egress.
[05:07] Alicia: regarding penetration testing — can we run our own blackbox pen test against the dedicated endpoint?
[05:14] Liam: yes, customers can run pen tests once they coordinate and sign the testing window; we also publish our pen test summary.
[05:22] Priya: timeline pressure — we need pricing and legal redlines by next Friday to hit our procurement window.
[05:28] Maya: understood. we'll push the security packet today, pricing scenarios by Wednesday, and Jordan will set up bench availability options.
[05:35] Ben: one more thing, embeddings store — we want to persist merchant embedding vectors in our own store, how would that integrate?
[05:42] Jordan: you can use Redwood's embeddings API or host a connector to push embeddings to your vector DB. for dedicated/private we can disable the managed embeddings store and provide a streaming hook to your DB.
[05:56] Alicia: on DPA items — subprocessor list: we need clarity on any third-party infra providers that handle logs.
[06:02] Maya: will include subprocessors in the security packet; typically cloud infra providers and monitoring vendors are listed.
[06:10] Carlos: legal question — data deletion: if we terminate, how quickly do you purge customer data and can we get a deletion certificate?
[06:18] Maya: standard is 30 days for deletion on hosted, immediate for dedicated/private depending on your configuration; we can issue a deletion certificate as part of contract.
[06:27] Priya: ok that helps procurement.
[06:30] Jordan: operational note: for low-latency payments you may want to colocate models, smaller sequence lengths, and active prefix caching—we can demo caching behavior during the bench.
[06:42] Ben: caching: will that leak data between tenants? that's a hard requirement.
[06:47] Jordan: shared caches are partitioned, and dedicated pools can have in-memory per-customer caches. we'll show memory isolation docs.
[06:56] Maya: quick housekeeping: I'll send links to the security packet, SOC 2 letter, and a sample MSA with typical redlines we accept.
[07:06] Priya: please also include a sample pricing card showing commit tiers and overage caps, we need that for our finance gate.
[07:12] Maya: noted.
[07:15] Liam: last bit — any competitors you're evaluating?
[07:18] Alicia: we've looked at Anthropic and Cohere; Anthropic's model choice is interesting but the ops story is not as mature for dedicated pools.
[07:27] Maya: understood. we'll highlight differences in the packet.
[07:30] Carlos: one contractual ask — we'll want an SLA credit table with breakpoints.
[07:35] Maya: we'll include a draft SLA schedule in the MSA attachment.
[07:40] Ben: for the bench, can Jordan use a small sample dataset with token length distribution and a burst profile?
[07:46] Jordan: yes please send a CSV of timestamps and token counts; Ben, if you can share by Tuesday we'll schedule bench mid next week.
[07:55] Priya: final check — procurement lead times: target signing 6 weeks from now if everything aligns.
[08:02] Maya: great, that's achievable if we move quickly.
[08:06] Wrap and recap.
